review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the indices in range(col, n) and mark the unique index p that Python's max call would select: abs(rows[p][col]) is not less than any later candidate value and is strictly greater than every earlier candidate value. A Grover-style procedure would only propose this pivot index; it would not replace elimination, back substitution, residual computation, or reporting.

Encode col, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 active-column values rows[i][col]. A reversible predicate must reproduce the relevant Python abs and comparison behavior, including first-index tie selection and any signed-zero or nonfinite intermediate behavior reachable during elimination. Coherent loading, floating-point representation, comparison circuits, workspace uncomputation, and their costs are unresolved.
Validated inputs begin as finite binary64 values, while the nominated statement consumes dynamically updated elimination state.

binding.rationale: The primary rule explicitly uses not-less against later values and strict-greater against earlier values. Preserve >= and literal not-< readings rather than select a favorable NaN interpretation. No explicit finite-state guard is given. The unchanged line13 nomination and structural assertion do not resolve the rule's behavior.

interpretations.meaning: Conventional >= reading of not-less for later values.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices if k > i) and all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i)

interpretations.meaning: Literal not-< reading for later values.
interpretations.expression: not any(values[i] < values[k] for k in indices if k > i) and all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i)
